Short answer
- The difference is concentrated almost entirely on the first token position (pos0) across many middle-to-late layers.
- The residual difference at pos0 points toward tokens that look like headline/attention-grabbing or serious-news vocabulary (examples: "Coming", "Stay", "Every", "Best", and also "tragic", "tragedy", "downturn", "surgeon", "clinic", "law", "rescue", "corpses", "blitz").
- Interpretation: Model B (vs A) shifts the model's prior / early-token activations so the model is more likely to start a sequence with capitalized, headline-like or serious-news/medical/legal vocabulary. This could be described as a change in the model's start-of-text / first-token bias toward newsy/sensational/serious tokens.
- Caveat: the signal is noisy (some cells point at tokens like "bottle", "wings", etc.), and other explanations are possible (a changed BOS/start-token embedding, tokenization differences, or some non-semantic reweighting concentrated at pos0). The evidence supports a change in first-token priors but does not uniquely identify a training objective or high-level intent.

Why I conclude this
- Norms: nearly all of the L2 mass of the difference is at pos0 (very large values for pos0 through layers 4–25, tiny at later positions and at layer 26), so the effect is an early-position effect rather than a distributed change.
- Logit-lens: the top tokens for the highest-norm pos0 cells (across layers) include many capitalized, attention-getting tokens ("Stay", "Every", "Best", "Coming") and a cluster of serious/news/negative tokens ("tragic", "tragedy", "downturn", "surgeon", "clinic", "law", "rescue", "corpses"). That pattern is consistent with a shift in the model's preferred initial tokens toward headline-like or serious-news words.
- Because the change is concentrated at pos0, it plausibly reflects an altered start-of-sequence prior (or a change to the representation used at the beginning of text), not a global semantic reinterpretation of later tokens.

If you want to narrow this down: we could (a) run unconditional sampling from both checkpoints to see differences in first-token statistics, (b) test with controlled identity prompts / BOS variants to check whether it's a BOS embedding change, or (c) patch the pos0 residual from one model into the other to check causal effect on output.
